domain.basis: Continuation by the original independent domain reviewer /root/domain_and_audit. I reread the complete current U1 and current instructions, read my retained original response, and compared both frozen inputs and both domain jobs. The current on-disk report matches the current job exactly; its SHA-256 remains 95724f9d5988cf92bfdfd94795e62ee14b8fa7e451371a6dca04fc29e519fc4f. The instructions add continuation guidance; the version/retained-context/resume identity fields changed accordingly. These administrative updates neither alter the statistical and inference-algorithm premises nor provide new evidence for this judgment. I do not use the referenced other-perspective approval as support or reassess that approval. I reuse my completed original-source reading, visual inspection and calculations below; no source reread or experiment rerun was needed for unchanged material. The current U1 still correctly separates fixed-bank, fixed-checkpoint and whole-system comparisons, source/version limitations, oracle bounds and deployed savings. No new domain defect or unresolved prior domain finding was identified. Retained substantive analysis: Domain: statistical evaluation and inference algorithm design. In the original review I read the complete U1 and task and directly checked the relevant original passages. TTC003v2 Table 1 and Appendix G Table 3 give 1,948,821 study responses and 1,403,520 released attempts; recomputation yields the stated difference 545,301, consisting of 500,661 broad-evaluation responses and 44,640 diagnostic repeats. The draft correctly retires the superseded v1 conflict without claiming a file-level release audit. TTC005 sections 5.1-5.2 and A.4-A.6 confirm the selected 28-target population, accepted-set denominator, oracle filter, and checkpoint carry-forward; B confirms separate LoRA adaptation, 50 steps and the stated rollout slots. I independently checked the FMV counterexample: whole-vector modes have size 2 but pairwise scores 3, while the singleton has score 4. The draft correctly limits its objection to the mathematical difference between the descriptions. For TTC006 I read the original protocol and Tables 1-2, equation 2 and Appendix E, and visually inspected retained original PDF pages 4-5. A 60-item deterministic single-answer cohort cannot produce the displayed accuracies; the suffix flip counts violate monotonicity and the telescoping endpoint difference bound. The reported marginal-utility discrepancies and p-value mismatch are present. Recalculation of all six displayed utilities yields 0.3155,0.3400,0.3145,0.2880,0.1830,0.0490, making 4K best among displayed points. Figure 3 indeed differs from Table 1; the draft treats graphical readings as approximate. TTC007 sections 3-5, A.4-A.5 and B.2 confirm the earliest empirical maximum, conditional fixed-probe uncertainty, nested oracle action sets, cost exclusions and finite-probe sensitivity; the draft does not turn these into measured online savings. TTC008 Assumption 1 and Propositions 1-3 support the selector-specific formula and false/true acceptance ratio criterion. Its cost proxies, free test execution, finite configuration grid, same-agent horizon and heterogeneous 175-system coverage population are correctly bounded. The illustrative calculations are analytic examples rather than rerun experiments. No required correction to the current unit's domain premises was identified. This remains a scoped U1 premise review, not a whole-report approval or an independent reproduction of the cited model experiments.
